focus: a complete KTZ-style dependency chain ending in one global polynomial and exponent $1-o(1)$

messages.body_markdown: `E2E-15H` imports the popularity-tail decoder, so the genuinely open incidence statement is now only `E2E-15L`, where $u_*\epsilon^2<2^{70}d$. Please target this exact low-tail, label-aware alternative: either decode directly or retain $\Omega_\theta(\epsilon)$ mass in a rank-reaching certificate with $D\le K_\theta d$.
messages.subject: Residual low-tail obligation isolated

messages.body_markdown: The pending synthesis `GENIUS:P2`–`P10` now states the exact generic closure package behind `E2E-16`–`E2E-23`: parameter gate, rank radicalization, extension, direct $B_Z$ cleanup, degree-$D$ peeling, component lift, divisor counting, and edge pigeonholing. Please audit this package standalone; the older accepted KTZ steps cover only the specialized cardinality-selected configuration.
messages.subject: Audit the common-relation closure package

messages.body_markdown: The bounded-weight conclusion $D=O_\theta(d)$ still has two independent uses: it makes the whole-relation cleanup and peeling loss $O_\theta(d/p)=o(\epsilon)$, and it bounds the component-template list by $\deg_ZB\le D/d=O_\theta(1)$. The new `GENIUS` evidence is pending, so this cleaner closure changes no verified proof status.
messages.subject: Bounded weight closes both losses

messages.body_markdown: `E2E-25` is now stated as the positive counterexample theorem and cites the proved modal construction, rather than citing a refuted universal claim as positive evidence. It rules out uniform $Cd/p$ recovery but remains below every fixed $(d/p)^{1-\eta}$ trigger.
messages.subject: Exact-linear guardrail normalized

nodes.label: Bivariate prime-field instance
nodes.notes: The scope is exactly $m=2$, prime field, and integer $100<d<p$.
nodes.statement_markdown: Fix a prime $p$, an integer $100<d<p$, a function $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$, and, for every affine line $L$, a bijective affine parametrization $\ell_L:\mathbb F_p\to L$ and a polynomial $P_L\in\mathbb F_p[t]$ with $\deg P_L\le d$. Put $$\rho=\frac dp,\qquad \operatorname{Agr}_d(f)=\max_{\deg_{\rm tot}Q\le d}\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)].$$

nodes.label: Accepted graph and completion predicate
nodes.notes: Normalized edge mass equals uniform line-versus-point acceptance probability.
nodes.statement_markdown: Define $$E_{\rm acc}=\{(\ell_L(t),L):P_L(t)=f(\ell_L(t))\},\qquad \epsilon=\frac{|E_{\rm acc}|}{p^2(p+1)}.$$ For an accepted subgraph $G=(X,T,E)$ put $$e(G)=\frac{|E|}{p^2(p+1)}.$$ For $c>0$, let $\mathsf{Done}_c$ mean that some $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ with $\deg_{\rm tot}Q\le d$ satisfies $$\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge c\epsilon.$$

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ component measures
nodes.notes: This starts the independently accepted component-level KTZ baseline.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $G=(X,T,E)$ be a connected accepted graph of minimum degree $k$, and put $\tau=|T|/[p(p+1)]$. If $$k^2\ge2^{40}dp,\qquad k^3\ge2^{40}d\tau p^2,$$ then $$\frac{|X|}{p^2}\ge\frac{k}{4p},\qquad \tau\ge\frac{k}{4p}.$$

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ reaching family
nodes.notes: The selector is cardinality-based and local to one component.
nodes.statement_markdown: Under `E2E-04`, there is $R\subseteq T$ such that $$\frac{4|T|}{k}\le|R|\le\frac{16|T|}{k},\qquad |R|\ge p+1,$$ and every $L\in T$ has more than $\deg_G(L)/2$ neighbors $x$ incident in $G$ to some $M\in R\setminus\{L\}$.

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ weighted interpolant
nodes.notes: Its degree depends on the reaching-family cardinality.
nodes.statement_markdown: Put $$D=16\left(\left\lfloor\sqrt{d|R|}\right\rfloor+1\right).$$ There is a nonzero squarefree $A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ with $\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}A\le D$, $A_Z\not\equiv0$, and $$A(\ell_M(t),P_M(t))\equiv0\qquad(M\in R).$$ Moreover, $D/k<1/5000$ and $D<k\le p<|R|$.

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ root extension
nodes.notes: More than $D$ reached roots force each remaining restriction identity.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every $L\in T$, $$A(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0.$$

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ characteristic-safe cleanup
nodes.notes: This is the independently accepted generic-direction cleanup.
nodes.statement_markdown: Write $A=HB$, where $H\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ is the coefficient content in $Z$. Then $B$ is squarefree and has total degree below $p$. There is a formal directional derivative $\mathcal D$ with $\gcd(B,\mathcal DB)=1$ and an exceptional set satisfying $$|E_{\rm exc}|\le pD^2+D|T|.$$ Outside $E_{\rm exc}$, the $B$-identity holds and $\mathcal DB$ is nonzero at every retained accepted incidence.

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ clean core
nodes.notes: The cleanup may fragment the original component.
nodes.statement_markdown: One has $$\frac{|E_{\rm exc}|}{|E|}<\frac1{4000}.$$ Peeling vertices below $k_1=\lfloor k/100\rfloor$ leaves a nonempty accepted graph $G_1$ of minimum degree at least $k_1$.

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ simple roots
nodes.notes: Two retained directions convert directional nonvanishing into vertical simplicity.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Every point vertex $x$ of $G_1$ satisfies $$B(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0.$$

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ component decoder
nodes.notes: The conclusion is one polynomial, not a list.
nodes.statement_markdown: Under `E2E-04`, there is one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that $$\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge\frac{k}{800p}.$$

nodes.label: Conditional square-root frontier
nodes.notes: Local agreement alone does not supply the required small-component hypothesis.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $k_0=\lfloor\epsilon p/100\rfloor$. If a component of the KTZ-pruned core has line measure $\tau\le\Lambda\epsilon$ and $$\epsilon\ge\sqrt{8{,}000{,}000\cdot2^{40}\Lambda}\left(\frac dp\right)^{1/2},$$ then $\mathsf{Done}_{1/160000}$ holds.

nodes.label: Verified integral-cover obstruction
nodes.notes: This forces a decoder alternative in any universal sparsification statement.
nodes.statement_markdown: For $p\ge103$ and $2\le K\le p/(100\log p)$, there is a legal constant-label table with $$\frac1{2K}\le\epsilon\le\frac2K$$ such that every line family reaching half of every accepted line has $$|R|\ge\frac{Kp}{16}\ge\frac{p}{32\epsilon},$$ while some constant polynomial has agreement at least $\epsilon/2$.

nodes.label: Connected graph-only obstruction
nodes.notes: The enclosing audit verdict is `revise`; this is a method barrier, not a soundness counterexample.
nodes.statement_markdown: At $\epsilon=d/p$ there is a connected full-support legal table attaining the point- and line-star lower envelopes, with every line of accepted degree $d$, every point of accepted degree $d$ or $d+1$, and perfect decoder $Q=0$. Its accepted graph is $K_{2,2}$-free, and for $0<\vartheta\le1$ its fractional other-line reaching optimum satisfies $$\frac{\vartheta p(p+1)}{d+1}\le\operatorname{OPT}_\vartheta\le\frac{\vartheta p(p+1)}{d-1}.$$

nodes.label: Rank-reaching relation interface
nodes.notes: The characteristic inequality $D<p$ is deliberately absent and is derived at `E2E-16`.
nodes.statement_markdown: For an integer $D\ge d$, put $$V_D=\{A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]:\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}A\le D\},$$ $$\Phi_{R,D}:V_D\to\bigoplus_{M\in R}\mathbb F_p[t]_{\le D},\qquad A\mapsto\bigl(A(\ell_M(t),P_M(t))\bigr)_{M\in R}.$$ A tuple $(G,R,D)$, where $G=(X,T,E)$ is a nonempty accepted subgraph, is rank-reaching if $R\subseteq T$, $|R|>D$, $$\operatorname{rank}\Phi_{R,D}<\dim V_D,$$ and every $L\in T$ has more than $D$ distinct neighbors $x$ for which $(x,M)\in E$ for some $M\in R\setminus\{L\}$.

nodes.label: Accepted point-popularity tail
nodes.notes: Universally $u_*\ge\lceil\epsilon(p+1)/2\rceil$; this alone recovers only the cubic scale.
nodes.statement_markdown: For $a_x=|\{L:(x,L)\in E_{\rm acc}\}|$ and $$\delta_j=\frac1{p^2(p+1)}\sum_{x:a_x\ge j}a_x,$$ define, when $\epsilon>0$, $$u_*=\max\{j\in\{1,\ldots,p+1\}:\delta_j\ge\epsilon/2\}.$$

nodes.label: High-popularity decoder branch
nodes.notes: The exact implication passed its line audit, but the enclosing source verdict is `revise`.
nodes.statement_markdown: If $$u_*\epsilon^2\ge2^{70}d,$$ then $\mathsf{Done}_{1/12800}$ holds.

nodes.label: Residual bounded-weight rank-or-decode dichotomy
nodes.notes: This is the principal open incidence bottleneck. It must be label-aware by `E2E-13` and `E2E-13R`.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For every fixed $0<\theta\le1/4$, there exist $C_\theta,K_\theta\ge1$ and $0<a_\theta,c_\theta\le1$ such that, if $$\epsilon\ge C_\theta\rho^{1-\theta},\qquad u_*\epsilon^2<2^{70}d,$$ then either $\mathsf{Done}_{c_\theta}$ holds or there is a rank-reaching tuple $(G,R,D)$ satisfying $$e(G)\ge a_\theta\epsilon,
\qquad d\le D\le K_\theta d.$$

nodes.label: Full bounded-weight dichotomy
nodes.notes: The inequalities defining the high- and low-tail cases are exhaustive.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Put $$\bar c_\theta=\min\{c_\theta,1/12800\}.$$ Whenever $$\epsilon\ge C_\theta\rho^{1-\theta},$$ either $\mathsf{Done}_{\bar c_\theta}$ holds or there is a rank-reaching $(G,R,D)$ with $$e(G)\ge a_\theta\epsilon,
\qquad d\le D\le K_\theta d.$$

nodes.label: Near-linear parameter and loss gate
nodes.notes: This arithmetic is exact in the pending synthesis and derives, rather than assumes, the characteristic bound.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Enlarge $C_\theta$ until $C_\theta\ge16K_\theta/a_\theta$. In the relation branch, with $q=D/p$, $$q\le\frac{K_\theta}{C_\theta}\epsilon\rho^\theta\le\frac{a_\theta\epsilon}{16}\le\frac1{16}.$$ Consequently, $$D<p,
\qquad q^2+3q\le4q\le\frac{a_\theta\epsilon}{4}.$$

nodes.label: Squarefree rank-kernel relation
nodes.notes: `GENIUS:P3` states the exact generic claim, but its independent audit is pending.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For the rank-reaching tuple in the relation branch, there is a nonzero squarefree $A\in V_D$ such that $$A_Z\not\equiv0,
\qquad A(\ell_M(t),P_M(t))\equiv0\quad(M\in R).$$

nodes.label: Rank-reaching root extension
nodes.notes: The accepted KTZ step supplies the root-count template; the exact abstract statement is pending in `GENIUS:P4`.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every line vertex $L\in T$, $$A(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0.$$

nodes.label: Whole-relation vertical cleanup
nodes.notes: The separability and resultant ingredients are independently accepted; the assembled generic package still awaits audit.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Write $A=HB$, where $H\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ is the coefficient content in $Z$. Put $$h=\deg H,
\qquad \delta=\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}B,
\qquad r=\deg_ZB,
\qquad \gamma=\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}B_Z.$$ Then $B$ is nonzero, squarefree, primitive, and $Z$-dependent, with $$h+\delta\le D,
\qquad \gamma\le\delta-d,
\qquad \gcd(B,B_Z)=1.$$ The number of content-trivial or identically $B_Z$-ramified lines is at most $$(r-1)\delta+r\gamma-dr(r-1)+h\le\frac{D^2}{d}-D.$$ There is $E_{\rm exc}\subseteq E$ such that $$\frac{|E_{\rm exc}|}{p^2(p+1)}\le\frac{D^2/d-D}{p(p+1)}+\frac{D-d}{p}<\left(\frac Dp\right)^2+\frac Dp.$$ Every line incident to $E\setminus E_{\rm exc}$ satisfies $B(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$, and every retained edge $(x,L)$ satisfies $$B(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0.$$

nodes.label: Global simple-root peeling
nodes.notes: Exceptional deletion costs less than $q^2+q$; peeling both shores at degree $D$ costs less than $2q$.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Starting from $(X,T,E\setminus E_{\rm exc})$, iteratively delete every point or line vertex of current degree at most $D$. The resulting nonempty accepted graph $G_1=(X_1,T_1,E_1)$ satisfies $$e(G_1)\ge\frac{a_\theta\epsilon}{2},
\qquad \operatorname{mindeg}(G_1)>D.$$ Every $L\in T_1$ satisfies $B(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$, and every $x\in X_1$ satisfies $$B(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0.$$

nodes.label: Componentwise whole-relation lift
nodes.notes: The older component statement has verdict `revise`; the exact generic version in `GENIUS:P8` is pending audit.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For every connected component $\Gamma$ of $G_1$, there is $Q_\Gamma\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ with $\deg_{\rm tot}Q_\Gamma\le d$ such that $$B(X,Y,Q_\Gamma(X,Y))\equiv0,
\qquad Q_\Gamma(x)=f(x)\quad(x\in X(\Gamma)).$$

nodes.label: Bounded component-template compression
nodes.notes: This is polynomial remainder followed by distinct monic divisor counting; its exact source audit is pending.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $\mathcal Q$ be the set of distinct polynomials $Q_\Gamma$. Then $$Z-Q(X,Y)\mid B(X,Y,Z)\qquad(Q\in\mathcal Q),$$ and therefore $$1\le|\mathcal Q|\le\deg_ZB\le\left\lfloor\frac Dd\right\rfloor\le K_\theta.$$

nodes.label: One-polynomial aggregation and fixed-theta closure
nodes.notes: No Vinh mixing is used; disconnected components with the same template are combined first.
nodes.statement_markdown:
In the relation branch, some $Q\in\mathcal Q$ carries a union $E_Q$ of component edge sets and a union $X_Q$ of component point sets such that $$Q=f\text{ on }X_Q,
\qquad \frac{|E_Q|}{p^2(p+1)}\ge\frac{e(G_1)}{|\mathcal Q|}\ge\frac{a_\theta\epsilon}{2K_\theta}.$$ Hence $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\frac{|X_Q|}{p^2}\ge\frac{|E_Q|}{p^2(p+1)}\ge\frac{a_\theta\epsilon}{2K_\theta}.$$ Together with the direct branch, $\mathsf{Done}_{c_\theta^*}$ holds for $$c_\theta^*=\min\left\{\bar c_\theta,\frac{a_\theta}{2K_\theta}\right\}.$$

nodes.label: Exact-linear counterexamples
nodes.notes: This refutes a uniform $Cd/p$ endpoint but lies below every fixed target trigger.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For every absolute $C,c>0$, there are arbitrarily large primes $p$ and legal instances with $d=101$ such that $$\epsilon\ge C\frac dp,
\qquad \operatorname{Agr}_d(f)<c\epsilon.$$

nodes.label: Singular-lift guardrail
nodes.notes: This shows why `E2E-19` must retain vertical simple roots.
nodes.statement_markdown: For $p>4d+1$ and $D=2d$, there is an absolutely irreducible $C\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ of weighted degree $D$ supporting more than $D$ distinct degree-at-most-$d$ graph lines, while no $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ satisfies $$C(X,Y,Q(X,Y))\equiv0.$$ Every vertically ramified lift on the supported graphs is singular.

nodes.label: Near-linear bivariate soundness
nodes.notes: For fixed $\eta>0$, take $\theta=\min\{\eta,1/4\}$; then $\rho^{1-\eta}\ge\rho^{1-\theta}$. The endpoint remains blocked on `E2E-15L`, and `GENIUS:P2`–`P12` remain pending independent audit.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $\eta>0$ there exist $C_\eta,c_\eta>0$ such that, for every prime $p$, every integer $100<d<p$, and every legal bivariate line table, $$\operatorname{Agr}_{\rm LVP}(f,P)\ge C_\eta\left(\frac dp\right)^{1-\eta}$$ implies that there is one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfying $$\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge c_\eta\operatorname{Agr}_{\rm LVP}(f,P).$$

summary: Round 4 preserves the independently accepted KTZ component chain `E2E-04`–`E2E-12` and separates its verified integral-cover obstruction from stronger revise-grade graph-only diagnostics. The popularity-tail theorem now removes the high-tail case, isolating the principal open incidence statement as the low-tail, label-aware obligation `E2E-15L`. Its required output remains exact: accepted mass $\Omega_\theta(\epsilon)$, formal rank deficiency, more than $D$ reached roots per line, and $D\le K_\theta d$. The relation branch then has a linear KTZ-style closure: derive $D<p$ and an absorbable loss budget; radicalize a kernel relation; extend it to all carrier lines; remove content and nonsimple $B_Z$ roots; peel to minimum degree above $D$; lift one polynomial on every component; compress all component polynomials to at most $\deg_ZB\le D/d$ divisors of the common relation; and pigeonhole edges to one global polynomial. `GENIUS:P2`–`P12` now state this generic package exactly but remain pending independent audit, so they do not change proof status. The unconditional corpus still stops at exponent $1/3$; the target remains blocked on `E2E-15L` and the pending audits of the generic algebraic transfer.
target_statement: Prove that soundness at least $(d/p)^{1-o(1)}$ yields agreement with one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial for $100<d<p$ over $\mathbb F_p$.
title: End-to-end soundness chain
